data.title: Studies of nephron regeneration after nephrectomy in Axolotl
data.description: Axolotls underwent partial nephrectomy and were then randomly divided into a control group and a TCP6-treated group. TCP6 is a peptide derived from Tenascin C. After two weeks post-nephrectomy, newly regenerated tissues from both control and TCP6-treated axolotls were collected. Kidney tissue from a sham group (non-nephrectomy) of axolotls was also extracted to serve as a baseline. To elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying TCP6-mediated renal regeneration, we conducted RNA sequencing on regenerating kidney tissues harvested at week 2 post-nephrectomy.

data.title: High-resolution annotation of axolotl transcriptome using long-read sequencing
data.description: Transcriptome studies on axolotls have provided crucial insights into their regenerative mechanisms. However, the annotation of the axolotl transcriptome has been incomplete, particularly regarding dynamically expressed transcripts. Current annotation efforts have relied on short-read sequencing, which falls short in resolving the complexity of the transcriptome due to the limited length of the sequence reads. To address these challenges, we employed the SMRT (Single Molecule Real-Time) sequencing platform to study the transcriptome of axolotl normal and regenerative organoids.
